text:
maria: Quick alert — canary-3 showing steady KV memory growth over 45m after the kernel-selection tweak (commit abc1234). Longctx sessions seem to be pinning pages and not releasing; fragmentation is spiking for a small set of tenants.
ankit: ugh. any pprof traces?
maria: yep pasted the top output below (trimmed):
```
(pprof) top
241.3MB  52.2%  page_cache         github.com/redwood/inference/kv.(*Page).Data
98.7MB   21.3%  page_meta          github.com/redwood/inference/kv.(*Shard).allocPageMeta
45.0MB    9.7%  slab_frag          github.com/redwood/inference/kv.(*Slab).fragmentation
Tags: tenant=ad_hoc_prod_42, seq_len>4096
```
maria: note most of the heavy pages are tagged with tenant=ad_hoc_prod_42 and longctx clients (chat sessions). The eviction scanner is scanning but fails to evict pinned pages, so other tenants get evicted and we see noisy-neighbor behavior.
kevin: does this line up with the kernel-selection change? that was supposed to favor reuse paths that avoid copies.
maria: timeline matches — new kernel picks fast-path that re-binds KV handles into the longctx path and sets a pin while the kv cursor is referenced by the runtime. We didn't account for long held cursors >5min.
sara: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) soft per-tenant residency watermark + async compaction when exceeded, 2) make pinned pages have an expiration token (e.g., 30s) unless actively touched.
ankit: (2) feels safer short-term. expiration avoids global stall. but we need careful correctness checks for cursor validity.
kevin: agree. also want better telemetry — add histogram of pin duration and count of eviction failures per tenant. then we can tune watermarks.
maria: added an experiment plan in the canary channel:
- add pin-expiry (config=kv.pin_expiry_ms) default 30s on canary-3
- expose per-tenant pin-duration metric (prom: kv_pin_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant=~".*"})
- if tenant_residency > warn_pct (e.g., 70%) fire alert
- short-term bump ad_hoc_prod_42 soft quota to reduce immediate evictions
ankit: can you post the minimal patch? i can run a quick review.
maria: patch link: https://git.redwood/inference/pull/5421
ci-bot: Build #5421 passed — deployed to canary-3 at 1732458900 :white_check_mark:
kevin: after deploy, i'm seeing fewer eviction errors but memory still climbs slowly. maybe fragmentation not solved by expiry alone.
sara: fragmentation suggests slab reuse isn't reclaiming freed slots — we should run a compact pass that merges small free extents periodically. compaction could be background at low priority.
ankit: background compaction + pin expiry seems reasonable. also consider proactively demoting longctx pins to lower priority after N tokens. we can instrument token counter in cursor.
maria: agreed. i'll add a compaction job that runs when a shard has >X% free-but-fragmented space and tenant_residency > Y. keeping it low-priority so CPU impact is minimal.
kevin: capture action items?
sara: action: maria to land pin-expiry + metrics (PR 5421) — pending monitor (ETA: 2h).
sara: action: ankit to prototype compaction worker that merges small free extents and exposes compaction_runs_total (ETA: 24h).
sara: action: kevin to add alert for eviction_failures_by_tenant > 5/min (ETA: 1h).
maria: i'll also add a short-run simulation harness that replays longctx traces to validate cursor-expiry correctness before wider rollout.
ankit: thumbs up. once we have metrics we can decide if we need per-tenant throttles or enforced pin budgets.
kevin: ping me if ad_hoc_prod_42 still causes >5% tail latency regressions after compaction.
ci-bot: Canary monitor snapshot at 1732460389: kv_pin_expiry_active=1, eviction_failures=3/min, canary_memory_growth=+12MB/10m (improved).
maria: thanks all — will post follow-ups in this thread with perf numbers. :thumbsup:
